source_contract.statement: This contract is audited only under the explicit user-adopted interpretation, recorded at gates/leveque-finite-volume/artifacts/session-20260908/user-transport-interpretation-20260908.json (SHA-256 26f16aeef42a0c7de4865c4c00e9ba223a9ae53604abf55da427171f6bf8e16b). The original source-only contract and its ambiguity remain preserved (SHA-256 3149d14809cae7c259d76638b606c5bd1f7e9fbdd906cdfd99ec3d0a920494ae). Original source account: For the one-dimensional scalar advection equation with constant real velocity ū, the selected passage asserts that q(x,t) = q̃(x − ūt) supplies solutions for any profile q̃, and that the profile travels at velocity ū without changing shape [printed p. 1, (1.2)-(1.3) and surrounding text]. The passage does not explicitly restrict profile regularity or state a solution sense for nonsmooth profiles. The book later verifies this form for smooth functions and expressly distinguishes classical differential solutions from discontinuous solutions treated through conservation or weak formulations [printed pp. 4-5, section 1.1.2; printed pp. 17-18, (2.13); printed pp. 215-216, section 11.11]. Consequently, the source fixes the translation formula and propagation claim, while leaving the exact function class and nonsmooth interpretation of its introductory 'any function' wording unresolved.
assumptions: The governing equation is the homogeneous, one-dimensional, constant-coefficient scalar advection equation q_t(x,t) + ūq_x(x,t) = 0. [Printed p. 1, introduction to (1.1), scalar specialization, and (1.2).]
The coefficient ū is constant. No positivity or nonzero condition is imposed on it in the selected passage. [Printed p. 1, paragraph introducing (1.2).]

The selected paragraph states no explicit regularity condition on q̃. Its later classical explanation expressly concerns smooth functions of the translated form. [Printed p. 1, text following (1.3); printed pp. 17-18, sentence spanning (2.13).]

The real space-time domain comes from the preceding system notation; the selected paragraph does not introduce a half-line time domain or finite spatial interval. [Printed p. 1, q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m following (1.1), and (1.2)-(1.3).]

Sufficient smoothness supports passage from integral conservation to the classical differential equation; discontinuities require a different solution interpretation. [Printed pp. 4-5, section 1.1.2; printed p. 17, derivation (2.8)-(2.10).]

The smooth translated-profile statement and characteristic explanation in Chapter 2 clarify the selected formula. The converse, initial-value uniqueness discussion, and finite-pipe boundary conditions are explanatory context, not additional conclusions selected here. [Printed pp. 17-18, section 2.1 and (2.13)-(2.15).]

Chapter 11 supplies weak-solution context through an integral identity tested against C₀¹ functions, but does not explicitly connect every unrestricted function q̃ in the Chapter 1 wording to a specified weak-solution function space. [Printed p. 1, text after (1.3); printed pp. 215-216, Definition 11.1 and following paragraph.]
Adopted interpretation: The translated field preserves geometric transport for every real-valued profile and every real constant speed.
Adopted interpretation: Classical solutionhood of the translated profile is characterized exactly by everywhere differentiability of the profile.
Adopted interpretation: Integral conservation is interpreted by finite-rectangle balance with ordinary real length measure, on exactly locally interval-integrable profiles.
Preserved limitation: The pinned PDF does not itself explicitly specify this complete analytic profile class; original source ambiguity and all earlier nonaccepted audits remain evidence.

Exact user reply: Adopt the explicit convention and audit under that recorded interpretation
quantifiers: A constant real scalar ū, serving as the advection velocity; the selected assertion is parametric in this constant, although it is not written with a formal universal quantifier. [Printed p. 1, scalar case and paragraph introducing (1.2).]

An arbitrary profile q̃, with real scalar values and real argument ξ as inherited from the scalar spatial setting; the explicit scope is 'for any function q̃(ξ)'. [Printed p. 1, (1.1), scalar specialization, and text following (1.3).]
Space x and time t, inherited as real variables from q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m, with m = 1 in the selected scalar case. [Printed p. 1, text following (1.1) and equations (1.2)-(1.3).]
The resulting scalar field q is specified by q(x,t) = q̃(x − ūt). [Printed p. 1, (1.3).]
